plain.text: Saul approved of Stephen's death. That day a great persecution broke out against the church in Jerusalem, and all except the apostles were scattered through Judea and Samaria. Godly men buried Stephen and mourned deeply. Saul began to destroy the church, going from house to house and dragging off men and women to prison.

Those who had been scattered preached the word wherever they went. Philip went down to a city in Samaria and proclaimed the Messiah there. Crowds paid close attention when they heard him and saw the signs he did. Evil spirits came out of many, and many who were paralysed or lame were healed. There was great joy in that city.

A man named Simon had practised sorcery there and amazed everyone, who called him "the Great Power of God". But when the people believed Philip's good news about God's kingdom and Jesus, they were baptised, and Simon himself believed and was baptised. When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had accepted God's word, they sent Peter and John. They prayed for the new believers to receive the Holy Spirit, because the Spirit had not yet come on any of them. Peter and John placed their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit. Simon offered them money for this power. Peter said, "May your money perish with you, because you thought you could buy the gift of God!" He told Simon to repent and pray. Simon asked them to pray for him.

An angel told Philip to go south to the desert road from Jerusalem to Gaza. There he met an Ethiopian official in charge of the queen's treasury, who had been to Jerusalem to worship. He was sitting in his chariot reading Isaiah. The Spirit told Philip to go to the chariot. Philip asked, "Do you understand what you are reading?" "How can I, unless someone explains it to me?" He was reading, "He was led like a sheep to the slaughter." He asked who the prophet was talking about. Philip began with that passage and told him the good news about Jesus. They came to some water, and the man said, "Look, here is water. What can stand in the way of my being baptised?" (Verse 37 is not in the earliest manuscripts.) They went down into the water and Philip baptised him. Then the Spirit took Philip away, and the official went on his way rejoicing. Philip preached in all the towns until he reached Caesarea.

summary.bigIdea: Persecution scatters the believers, and the good news spreads to Samaria and to an Ethiopian official.
points: Saul persecutes the church, but the scattered believers preach wherever they go.
Samaritans believe and receive the Holy Spirit; Simon learns God's gift cannot be bought.
Philip explains Isaiah to an Ethiopian official, who is baptised and goes on his way rejoicing.
summary.reflection: The Ethiopian asked, "How can I... unless someone guides me?" Who helps you understand the Bible, or who could you help?
